About Me

Where power systems meet machine learning

I'm a Computer Science Engineering student who got pulled into the world of power systems research through two internships at NIT Puducherry's Department of Electrical & Electronics Engineering — and never looked back. What started as writing code for simulations turned into co‑authoring a research paper on a novel adaptive activation function for Graph Neural Networks that forecasts transmission line ampacity.

Outside of research, I build full‑stack web applications and enjoy translating dense technical ideas — thermal ratings, graph convolutions, adaptive gradients — into interfaces and tools that are actually usable. I hold an Advanced Diploma in Java Programming (A+, 91%) from GTech Computer Education, and I'm continually adding Python, ML frameworks, and modern web tooling to that base.
